svg.title: The Dead Spot — Where Nothing Is Looking
svg.desc: A simplified, small-size Zumo illustration has three proximity detector cones with uncovered blind wedges between the front and side directions. A three-step sequence shows an object being seen by the left detector, disappearing in the blind gap during a turn, and then being detected by the front detector. All labels and instructional overlays remain live SVG text and vectors.
svg.text: THE DEAD SPOT — WHERE NOTHING IS LOOKING
Three cones do not add up to a circle. Between “ahead” and “beside” there is a wedge no detector covers.
Two blind wedges, roughly 19° to 72° off each side of the nose.
Keep turning — FRONT picks it up.
Step 2 is not a broken sensor. It is the gap.
If a reading drops to 0 while you are turning toward the thing you just detected, the sensor is fine. Nothing is aimed there.
Design for it: remember what you saw, and keep turning. Lesson 10 leans on exactly this.
